root_cause: The bounded-yield forecast EXISTS is correlated to each outer Conversation. PostgreSQL executes a channels_message scan once per outer conversation, and the scan's work grows with the pending Message population.
measurement_boundary: PostgreSQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE Execution Time; 5 warmups and 30 repetitions per point; real compiled ORM SQL

messages_matrix.classification: approximately linear over the material range, with plan and cache noise; cost increases materially while loops stay fixed

conversations_matrix.classification: roughly linear to mildly superlinear in this measured range; multi-second selector polls at 500-1000 conversations

organizations_matrix: not run because independent Messages and Conversations matrices identify the causal mechanism sufficiently

explain_conclusion.dominant_node: forecast correlated channels_message Seq Scan in this synthetic corpus; the historical PROFILE chose Bitmap Heap Scan for the same repeated Message work
explain_conclusion.loops_determined_by: outer Conversation rows evaluated by the forecast, plus the three constant historical conversations in A/B; not by Organizations or Message count
explain_conclusion.sort: quicksort, maximum 25 kB in representative plans
explain_conclusion.heap_fetches: not reported for the dominant Seq Scan

relation_to_formal_profile: The corrected mixed case gives p50 97.990 ms and a representative 101.214 ms EXPLAIN, near the formal p50 97.497 ms and 127.583 ms plan. It does not reproduce PROFILE's p95/p99/max 291.922/422.705/622.632 ms because concurrency, data shape and worker conditions differ.
risk: At fixed 2000 pending Messages, 500 and 1000 Conversations require about 2.3 and 4.9 seconds p50 per selector SQL invocation. The repeated scan can delay polling under a plausible accumulated backlog regardless of the formal PROFILE threshold.
